why_this_matters: Day 167 sits in Phase 10 (Machine Learning), whose goal is: Train, tune, evaluate and explain supervised models from first principles. Today's core material - Standardisation vs normalisation vs robust scaling, When distance-based models need scaling, One-hot, ordinal, target and binary encoding - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: 3. Robust scalar
code.code:
from sklearn.preprocessing import RobustScaler
# Sample data with outliers
data = {'awen_numbers': [10, 20, 30, 1000, 50]}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
# Robust Scaling
scaler = RobustScaler()
df['awen_numbers_scaled'] = scaler.fit_transform(df[['awen_numbers']])
print(df)

code.heading: Ordinal Encoding
code.code:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
# Sample data
data = {'Size': ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large', 'Medium']}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df)

# Ordinal Encoding
ordinal_encoder = OrdinalEncoder(categories=[['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']])
df['Size_encoded'] = ordinal_encoder.fit_transform(df[['Size']])
print(df)

code.heading: 4. Logrithmic scaling/ Normalization
code.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

#random data with outliers
data = {'awen_numbers': [10000, 20000, 30000, 1000000, 50000]}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Log Transform
df['awen_numbers_log'] = np.log(df['awen_numbers'])
df['awen_numbers_log2'] = np.log2(df['awen_numbers'])
df['awen_numbers_log10'] = np.log10(df['awen_numbers'])
df.head()

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Standardisation vs normalisation vs robust scaling on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
